mrr.name: Monthly recurring revenue
mrr.definition: Monthly-normalized recurring subscription revenue from active paying accounts at the cutoff.
mrr.formula: Sum recurring subscription value per month across eligible accounts.
mrr.population: Active paid subscriptions at the reporting cutoff.
mrr.period: Point-in-time snapshot with a monthly run rate.
mrr.notes: Exclude one-time fees, free plans and taxes. Document treatment of discounts, delinquency, usage and FX. Keep MRR separate from recognized revenue.

arr.name: Annualized recurring revenue
arr.definition: Annualized recurring run rate at a reporting cutoff.
arr.population: Same account and revenue scope as MRR.
arr.notes: Distinguish annualized run rate from contracted ARR, recognized annual revenue and bookings.

mrr-growth.name: MRR growth
mrr-growth.definition: Relative change between comparable MRR snapshots.
mrr-growth.population: Same revenue basis, account eligibility, product scope and FX convention.
mrr-growth.notes: For a zero or negative baseline, report levels and absolute change. Explain changes in scope or measurement.

logo-churn.name: Paid customer churn
logo-churn.definition: Share of the opening paid customer cohort that lost its last paid subscription and had no reactivation before period end.
logo-churn.formula: 100 × opening-cohort customers churned by period end ÷ opening paid customer count.
logo-churn.population: Distinct paying customer accounts active at period start.
logo-churn.period: One closed reporting period, usually a month.
logo-churn.denominator: Distinct paying customer accounts active at period start.
logo-churn.notes: Confirm cancellation, delinquency, and reactivation timing. Stripe's 30-day subscriber churn includes new subscribers in its denominator. Keep that series distinct under this default.

nrr.name: Net revenue retention
nrr.definition: Closing recurring revenue from the opening customer cohort as a share of its opening recurring revenue.
nrr.formula: 100 × closing MRR from the opening cohort ÷ opening cohort MRR.
nrr.population: Customers with eligible recurring revenue at the start of the period.
nrr.period: One closed reporting period with matching cohort and FX rules.
nrr.notes: Include changes from expansion, contraction and churn in the opening cohort. Exclude new customers. NRR can exceed 100%.

grr.name: Gross revenue retention
grr.definition: Recurring revenue retained from the opening cohort with expansion excluded.
grr.formula: 100 × (opening MRR − contraction MRR − churn MRR) ÷ opening MRR.
grr.population: Customers with eligible recurring revenue at the start of the period.
grr.period: One closed reporting period with matching cohort and FX rules.
grr.notes: Exclude new business and expansion. Use consistent treatment of within-period churn and reactivation.

arpa.name: Average recurring revenue per account
arpa.definition: Average monthly recurring revenue per distinct paid account.
arpa.formula: MRR ÷ number of distinct paid accounts at the same cutoff.
arpa.population: Distinct paid accounts included in MRR.
arpa.denominator: Distinct paid accounts at the MRR cutoff.
arpa.notes: Separate account and user measures. Use one matching product and plan population.

cac.name: Customer acquisition cost
cac.definition: Average acquisition cost per new paying customer.
cac.formula: Eligible sales and marketing acquisition costs ÷ acquired paying customers.
cac.population: New paying customers in the attributed acquisition population.
cac.period: A defined acquisition window with spend aligned to the acquired cohort.
cac.denominator: New paying customers attributable to the included acquisition spend.
cac.notes: State which payroll, commissions, tools and channel costs are included. Align sales-cycle lag. Distinguish blended and channel CAC.

cac-payback.name: CAC payback period
cac-payback.definition: Estimated months for acquisition cost to be recovered from gross profit.
cac-payback.formula: CAC per acquired customer ÷ monthly gross profit per customer in the same acquired cohort.
cac-payback.population: The acquired customer cohort represented by CAC.
cac-payback.period: Cohort-based estimate using a monthly gross profit amount.
cac-payback.denominator: Monthly gross profit per customer in the same acquired cohort.
cac-payback.notes: Match account grain and currency. If margins or revenue change materially, use cumulative cohort gross profit to estimate payback.

gross-margin.name: Gross margin
gross-margin.definition: Gross profit as a share of recognized revenue.
gross-margin.formula: 100 × (recognized revenue − cost of goods sold) ÷ recognized revenue.
gross-margin.population: Revenue and directly attributable costs on the same product and recognition basis.
gross-margin.period: Same closed accounting period for revenue and costs.
gross-margin.denominator: Recognized revenue in the measured population and period.
gross-margin.notes: Use the Finance definition of cost of revenue. Explain scope of support, infrastructure, and service delivery costs.

ltv.name: Customer lifetime value
ltv.definition: Estimated lifetime gross profit per customer under a stable churn model.
ltv.formula: Monthly ARPA × gross margin as a fraction ÷ monthly customer churn as a fraction.
ltv.population: Comparable customer segment measured consistently in ARPA, margin and churn.
ltv.period: Monthly inputs with a shared population and period basis.
ltv.denominator: Monthly customer churn as a fraction.
ltv.notes: Label this an estimate. A zero denominator or unstable retention makes the simple model unsuitable. State whether LTV refers to revenue or gross profit.

ltv-cac.name: LTV to CAC ratio
ltv-cac.definition: Estimated lifetime gross profit relative to unit acquisition cost.
ltv-cac.formula: LTV per customer ÷ CAC per customer for the same segment.
ltv-cac.population: Same acquired audience, account grain and channels on both sides.
ltv-cac.period: Consistent acquisition cohort and currency basis.
ltv-cac.denominator: CAC per customer in the matched segment or cohort.
ltv-cac.notes: State LTV assumptions. Flag zero CAC, mismatched cohorts, and changes in acquisition-cost allocation.
